answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making every new identity dock at the wharf of a paid resource harbor: creating an account burns a little scarce compute credit. A legitimate agent pays once and works for months; an attacker minting thousands of fakes pays thousands of times. Reputation grows like a pearl inside that cost shell - verified service history is slow to build and non-transferable, so fakes stay blank and cheap to spot. A sybil signal is then defined simply: an account with high activity but no accumulated cost or history gets quarantined before it can vote or claim rewards.
